title: Real-Time Neuroadaptive Control with Tactile Calibration for Physical Human-Robot Interaction
content: We present a neuroadaptive control framework applied to a tactile sensing interface that enables real-time, human-guided physical interaction with a robotic arm. A dual-loop controller is employed, consisting of a real-time inner-loop neural network that compensates for nonlinear robot dynamics and an outer-loop adaptive admittance model that maps tactile sensor voltages to desired end-effector trajectories. Piezoresistive tactile sensors placed on the robot end-effector are individually calibrated using Auto-Regressive Moving Average (ARMA) models updated through Recursive Least Squares (RLS). To validate the robustness of the framework across user variability, twenty-eight human subjects conducted experiments to calibrate the sensors to their preferences, generating 112 unique calibration models. After calibration, physical interaction experiments were conducted to evaluate how well each user was able to follow pre-defined trajectories. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed calibration procedure achieves millimeter-level prediction accuracy (mean RMSE ≈ 2.70 mm across subjects) and enables effective human-guided robot motion during the rectangle calibration task. Furthermore, the average nearest-path tracking error improved from 11.07±5.45 mm in the initial trial to 8.41±3.48 mm in the final trial, indicating that users quickly learn to improve their guidance of the arm, while the neuroadaptive controller maintains stable trajectory tracking performance. These results demonstrate that the proposed calibration and control framework provides an intuitive physical interface between humans and robots while relying only on low-cost tactile sensing hardware rather than more expensive torque sensing methods.
